hero.title: All your coding agents. One window.
hero.lede: Polyvibe is a native macOS app for running several Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity sessions side by side, without losing track of any of them. Free and open source.
pain.title: Six terminals, three repos, two agents. Which one is waiting for you?
pain.text: When you run several agents at once, the hard part isn't the code. It's knowing where each one stands, which one is stuck, and which branch it's on. Polyvibe keeps all of that in order for you.
features.title: Built for people who always have four agents on the go
features.lede: Each session keeps its own folder, agent, terminal and history. You switch between them without restarting anything.
tasks.title: Your sessions become a task list
tasks.text: To do, running, waiting, done: every session has a status, and the sidebar shows at a glance what's moving and what's waiting. Group them by project, sort them by hand, archive them without ever losing anything.
card.quit.title: Quit, they keep going
card.quit.text: Agents can keep running while the app is closed. When you reopen it, each one is on screen just as you left it.
card.reply.title: Reply without switching sessions
card.reply.text: A background session has a question? Answer it from a palette, without leaving what you're doing.
card.templates.title: Prompt templates
card.web.title: Terminals and a web view per session
card.web.text: A terminal drawer for the server and logs, and a web view the agent can drive: open, read the console, take screenshots.
card.endpoint.title: Your models, your endpoints
card.endpoint.text: Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter or your company's gateway: Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity drives the model of your choice, tested before the first session.
card.a11y.title: Keyboard and VoiceOver
card.guard.title: The web view asks first
card.local.title: Everything stays on your Mac
card.local.text: No account, no telemetry. An endpoint's key stays in your keychain, and the app never lowers your CLIs' permissions.
keys.title: Everything is a shortcut away
keys.p: Find a session by ticket number, MR URL or branch.
keys.j: Open the session's terminal drawer, in its folder.
keys.u: See time and tokens used, by session, agent or model.
oss.title: Free, open, and built in public
oss.lede: The code is on GitHub, every architecture decision is documented there, and the roadmap is decided in the issues.
oss.adr: Published architecture decisions, from session storage to the terminal.
oss.agents: Supported agents: Claude Code, Codex CLI and Antigravity, on their own service or on an endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter…).
support.title: Polyvibe is free. A tip helps it grow.
support.lede: No paid tier, no ads, no data collected. If the app saves you time, you can support its development. Every contribution pays for time spent on your issues.
support.sponsors_text: Monthly or one-time, from $1. GitHub takes no commission.
final.title: Take back control of your agents
cl.title: What's new
cl.lede: Every Polyvibe release, what it adds and what it fixes. Numbers link to GitHub issues.
cl.notes_language: Release notes are written in French.
contrib.title: Polyvibe moves at the pace of your issues
contrib.lede: A bug that bugs you, a missing workflow, a half-formed idea: open an issue. Every release is built from what users write there.
contrib.bug.title: Something doesn't work
contrib.bug.text: The more precise, the faster it's fixed.
contrib.bug.l1: What you did, what you expected
contrib.idea.title: Something's missing
contrib.idea.text: Describe the situation rather than the solution.
contrib.idea.l1: What you were trying to do
contrib.code.title: You want to dig in
contrib.code.text: Swift 6, SwiftUI, and a documented architecture.
contrib.code.l1: Pick an open issue and say so in a comment
contrib.code.l2: The README explains how to build and test
contrib.any_language: Write in whatever language you like.
contrib.flow.title: What happens to your issue
contrib.flow.s1.title: It's read and triaged
contrib.flow.s1.text: Bug, improvement or question: it gets a label and, if needed, a few questions.
contrib.flow.s2.title: It's designed in public
contrib.flow.s2.text: The design proposal is written as a comment on the issue, before a single line of code.
contrib.flow.s3.title: It ships in a release
contrib.flow.s3.text: The pull request references the issue, and the changelog mentions it on release.

support.liberapay_text: By card, SEPA direct debit or PayPal. A French non-profit that takes no commission.
perso.title: Describe it, an agent makes it
perso.lede: The avatar that alerts you and the theme of your conversations each take one sentence. The app checks every result before keeping it, and everything can be exported.
avatar.title: An avatar that gives you a wave
avatar.text: When a session is waiting for your answer and you're in another app, your avatar pops up on top with the question. You reply without going back to Polyvibe. Codex draws it with its ten expressions in about a minute, or you import your own.
avatar.prompt: A small red fox in a navy blue hoodie, soft 3D illustration style, big expressive eyes, looking curious and friendly.
theme.title: A theme that suits you
theme.text: Six themes come built in. For your own, describe the mood: Claude Code or Codex picks the colors, the fonts and even the background picture. Each version applies live, contrast is checked so everything stays readable, and you can export it.
theme.prompt_dark: A dark forest-at-night theme: deep greens, an amber accent, and a misty forest at dusk in the background.
theme.prompt_light: Japanese paper: cream background, black ink, a touch of vermilion, a serif font and ink-wash mountains in the background.
avatar.shot_alt: The Polyvibe floating panel: the avatar and its speech bubble, showing an agent's request with Allow and Deny buttons.
theme.shot_alt: A Polyvibe conversation in a personal theme, with its own colors, font and background picture.
coord.title: One agent shares the work out between several sessions
coord.text: Turn on “Coordinate” and ask in a sentence: the session creates a child session per task, each in its own folder or worktree, writes to them, reads their answers and reports back. Children stay sessions like any other, linked to their coordinator in the sidebar, and their requests always wait for you in the palette.
coord.shot_alt: A coordinator session in the Polyvibe sidebar, linked by a line to its three child sessions.
card.archive.title: Archiving in one sentence
card.archive.text: “Every Friday, archive what has been done for two days.” An agent turns it into a rule, tested before it acts; each batch gets its report, summarized if you wish.
card.companion.title: The iPhone companion
card.companion.text: Follow your sessions and allow a command from your iPhone, through iCloud and with no server. In testing on TestFlight, for Macs with Apple silicon.
card.context.title: Effort and context in sight
card.accounts.title: Several accounts per agent
card.accounts.text: Your personal subscription and your work one, side by side: each Claude Code or Codex account has its own configuration folder, and is picked like an agent when you create a session.
thread.title: Reply to a paragraph, bookmark what matters
thread.text: Hover over a paragraph of the agent, or select a few words: “Reply” quotes them word for word ahead of your message, as in a thread. A bookmark in the margin marks a message, and the overview draws the whole conversation in small in place of the scroll bar: one click takes you there.
devices.title: The simulator beside the agent that codes the app
devices.text: iOS simulators, Android emulators and Android phones plugged into the Mac open live in a tab of the web view, driven with the mouse. The agent can open them itself, and the iPhone companion shows them by touch.
card.handover.title: Switch agents without losing the thread
card.handover.text: When you change agent or model, continue the conversation, or start a new one with the whole history, or with a summary you read before it is sent.
card.run.title: Run in one click
card.run.text: The “! …” command the agent leaves you, or its link to a .command script, becomes a Run button, on the Mac as on the iPhone.
card.auto.title: Fewer interruptions
card.auto.text: Codex and Antigravity can approve their own actions inside their sandbox: one setting per agent, per account and per endpoint.

card.agents.title: Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity
card.agents.text: Each session runs the agent of your choice, with your account and its models. It resumes the conversation exactly where it stopped, and every tool it calls reads clearly in the thread.
